candidate.title: scRC-Seq
candidate.scope: The middle row labelled scRC-Seq (single-cell retrotransposon capture sequencing) in the assigned Illumina schematic, interpreted as the Upton et al. 2015 nuclear-DNA workflow. Its left illustrations identify novel retrotransposition events and a retrotransposon binding site in genomic DNA; they are explanatory target cartoons, with no drawn material-transfer arrows into the preparation route. The connected route is Cell suspension → FACS isolation → Pick nuclei → Nucleus → Whole-genome amplification → Create sequencing library → Sequence capture → Enriched library. Adjacent sci-MET and scChIP-Seq rows are separate catalogue context. MALBAC is the paper-supported WGA component, not an additional target method. Paper-only WGS quality control, internal reaction splits/pools, sequencing and validation are not additional depicted branches or operations.

states.label: Enriched library
features: The selected product is a DNA sequencing library enriched for retrotransposon-end/host-genome junctions, rather than retrotransposon RNA or capture-probe sequences as the biological readout.
The final cartoon retains the internal target mark and both library terminal segments; it is drawn without the capture support.

In the cited implementation, L1-derived sequence connected to adjacent host DNA supplies the insertion-to-genomic-locus association. Junction-spanning reads can identify candidate nonreference L1 integration sites.

The genomic junction is carried by the DNA insert; source-nucleus identity is retained through the separately prepared, barcoded library in the primary implementation. The probe enriches that insert rather than replacing it as the sequenced target.
Enrichment is not exclusive to newly acquired insertions; reference and polymorphic L1 copies are also detectable.

operations.label: Sequence capture
operations.description: Select target-bearing fragments from the sequencing library by probe hybridization and affinity capture, producing an enriched DNA library. The short target-associated mark and tether to a gray support are depicted capture components, not another biological sample or a separate workflow.
operations.mechanism: The matched paper resolves the capture interface as LNA probes complementary to the extreme 5′ and 3′ L1-Ta ends. Their 5′ biotin modification permits capture with streptavidin beads. This describes the probe/support roles within the single drawn capture block.
operations.information_effect: Enriches DNA fragments physically linking an L1 end to adjacent host DNA. Subsequent paired-end junction-spanning reads can map candidate integration sites. In this capture design, typical L1 insertions can be detected at a 3′ junction, while the 5′ probe detects full-length or heavily 5′ truncated insertions retaining its binding sequence; either or both junctions may be recovered. Enrichment also retains reference and polymorphic targets. Capture alone does not establish that an insertion is somatic or authentic; the paper uses sample comparisons and artifact filtering/validation.
